My best prediction is that a typical employee would **hold this box by entering an unauthorised extension, then release the other 59 boxes on time**. They would probably document the reason and flag it to the manager.

The decisive facts are that the contents are irreplaceable, an authorised collector has a confirmed appointment only two days away, and destruction is irreversible. The centre has also already checked the collector’s authority and booked that appointment, which would likely make the employee feel some responsibility for preserving the box.

The manager’s instruction and certain audit scrutiny make this a consequential rule breach, so the prediction is not confident. Nevertheless, I’d expect many employees to accept an explainable €22 exception rather than knowingly destroy the only family letters and photographs just before collection.

That is a prediction of behaviour, not a claim that the extension is permitted. Tuesday’s approval could not retroactively authorise Monday’s change.
